answer: To resist Sybil attacks, agents anchor identity in cryptographic attestation chains verified via zero-knowledge proofs. A validating node will harbor no counterfeit identity when each credential acts as an encrypted cipher proving unique hardware execution. To deter swarms, registration requires a dynamic stake where attacker costs scale at an exponential rate $O(2^n)$, creating a plume of capital exhaustion that renders swarm synthesis economically ruinous.
